No confirmed malicious supply-chain compromise indicators — overall risk: info.

Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators found.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • In the provided text, there is no evidence of .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, install-time setup.py logic, PEP 517 build hooks, or code that runs automatically on installation or interpreter startup.
  • The curl | sh, systemctl, .bashrc edits, and Docker configuration snippets in README/PKG-INFO appear to be documented manual installation steps, not package-install automatic execution.
  • GStreamer pipeline examples and user-invoked commands were not treated as automatic execution paths.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Stealth

  • **Credential harvesting:** No evidence of broad discovery or collection of environment variables, .env files, SSH keys, cloud credentials, CI/CD tokens, GitHub/PyPI/npm tokens, or similar secrets.
  • **Archive staging / exfiltration:** No evidence of archiving, staging harvested files, or uploading them to attacker infrastructure.
  • **Network/Webhook:** pyml_alert webhook/MQTT and Kafka examples appear to be explicitly user-configured application functionality, with no evidence tying them to secret theft or covert exfiltration.
  • **Persistence:** The .bashrc update and systemd/Docker configuration snippets in README/PKG-INFO appear to be manual setup documentation for GStreamer plugin paths and NVIDIA Docker runtime configuration, not malicious persistence.
  • **Lateral movement:** No evidence of Kubernetes abuse, CI token theft, cloud metadata access, Docker socket abuse, or GitHub Actions workflow injection.
  • **Obfuscation/loader:** Many pre-scan eval hits appear to be PyTorch model.eval() false positives. Based on the provided evidence, there is no confirmed exec/eval loader, base64/zlib/marshal staging, or downloader dropper.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • Based on the provided manifest and text, there is no evidence supporting hidden payloads, unexplained native binaries, typosquatting, wheel/sdist mismatch, or sudden malicious dependency insertion.
  • The presence of plugins/python/gst_python_ml.egg-info may be generated sdist metadata and is not, by itself, a malicious distribution-integrity anomaly.

Further Verification Needed

  • The corpus shown is mainly limited to PKG-INFO and README.md out of 106 files; full review of pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, all Python modules, Dockerfiles, tests, and data files is needed.
  • If a wheel artifact exists, compare it against the sdist for file or behavior differences.
  • Full file listing and hash-based inspection are needed to rule out large model files, binaries, or hidden files.
